title: test-0070-MAT-DATAHANDLING
passage: In the village of Mathpur, the local library tracks how many books children borrow each week. This week, the record shows the following numbers: 0, 5, 5, 8, and 12. To understand the library's popularity, the librarian creates a bar graph. On the vertical axis, each small grid square represents 2 books, not just 1. He carefully ensures the axis starts exactly at zero to keep the visual ratios accurate. When calculating the average number of books borrowed, he includes the zero in his sum, knowing it is a valid data point that affects the total count. Finally, he looks at the most frequent number of books borrowed. Since the number 5 appears twice while others appear only once, he identifies 5 as the mode. He reminds the students that the mean does not have to be one of the numbers in the set, as it is just a calculated average. By organizing data this way, the librarian helps everyone see the true trends in reading habits across the village, ensuring no information is ignored or misrepresented in the charts.
summary: When calculating the average number of books borrowed, he includes the zero in his sum, knowing it is a valid data point that affects the total count. Finally, he looks at the most common number of books borrowed.
